{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Admiral's Men (also called the Admiral's company, more strictly, the Earl of Nottingham's Men; after 1603, Prince Henry's Men; after 1612, the Elector Palatine's Men or the Palsgrave's Men) was a playing company or troupe of actors in the Elizabethan and Stuart eras.","title":"Admiral's Men"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It is generally considered the second most important acting troupe of English Renaissance theatre (after the company of Shakespeare, the Lord Chamberlain's or King's Men).","title":"Admiral's Men"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The 2011 Hotan attack was a bomb-and-knife attack that occurred in Hotan, Xinjiang, China on July 18, 2011.","title":"2011 Hotan attack"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" According to witnesses, the assailants were a group of 18 young Uyghur men who opposed the local government's campaign against the full-face Islamic veil, which had grown popular among older Hotan women in 2009 but were also used in a series of violent crimes.","title":"2011 Hotan attack"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The men occupied a police station on Nuerbage Street at noon, killing two security guards with knives and bombs and taking eight hostages.","title":"2011 Hotan attack"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The attackers then yelled religious slogans, including ones associated with Jihadism, as they replaced the Chinese flag on top of a police station with another flag, the identity of which is disputed.","title":"2011 Hotan attack"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"The Admiral's Men occupied which kind of theatre in the 1590s ?"}
